scope: Preselected heldout8, seed42, step400. Assistant visual inspection of nine equal-index frames; process observations, not quantitative physics scores.

viewed.observation: Both generated paint streaks descend and change shape much faster than the real sampled clip. Candidate has no clear visible advantage in this panel.
Both generated cups fill quickly. Candidate and baseline surface disturbances differ; no clear overall advantage from this panel.

Both presses compress the car. Baseline progressively flattens a largely intact car; candidate develops an opening and stronger rear/body deformation early, then changes less. Real clip has slower roof compression followed by rear opening. Need continuous playback for contact and fragmentation; cannot label one better solely by amount of deformation.

Real ice visibly shrinks and nearly disappears. Candidate remains similar in size across most frames; baseline spreads the lower boundary but does not faithfully shrink the core. This is an unresolved physical transformation, not a diversity achievement.

Real clip has a propagating domino collapse and leaves fallen pieces. Baseline shows larger rearrangements including displaced groups; candidate retains more of the layout but does not clearly complete the propagating fall. More motion or more stability separately is insufficient.

Both maintain a flame. Baseline changes its outline/intensity more; candidate is steadier, closer to the steady reference in the sampled frames. This single steady case cannot establish general physical improvement.
Real clip shows blue liquid rising into the inverted bottle. Both candidate and baseline leave the bottle largely clear, missing the requested material transfer despite stable scene appearance.

All contain a water surface. Real clip has evolving rises and troughs, baseline has larger surface-level evolution, and candidate shows less progression. Exact waves need not match the real clip, but sampled appearance alone cannot establish physical temporal consistency.

conclusion: Representation collapse is reduced, but a robust generation benefit is not established. Continue paired generation and content controls; prioritize process completion and state consistency.
